_README: Copy to athlete/constants.json at the END of intake, not before — see the warning in SETUP.md §2 and the one in skills/intake/SKILL.md. Every athlete-specific number the code needs lives here; nothing in scripts/ or src/ may hardcode a value about the athlete (docs/INVARIANTS.md X-11). The validator requires the fields marked REQUIRED and will fail the build without them. Fill only what this athlete's domains actually need: a key nobody's goals need is a chore the coach invented (CLAUDE.md §1.1), and an unused section is better deleted than filled with a plausible number.

athlete._pronouns_note: The athlete's own, asked for at intake. they/them is the default until they say otherwise — never inferred from a name.
athlete._sex_REQUIRED: "male" or "female". Input to the Mifflin-St Jeor RMR equation ONLY: male adds +5, female subtracts 161 — a 166 kcal/day difference that is invisible on screen if wrong. It is used for nothing else. If no domain needs energy expenditure, it still must be set for the validator; the number simply goes unused.
athlete._dob_REQUIRED: YYYY-MM. Year-month is enough — age moves RMR by 5 kcal/year, so day precision would be false precision. Age is derived, never stored, so it cannot go stale.
athlete._timezone_note: An IANA zone, and it must be the ATHLETE's. Every row's date is derived from it (data/METHOD.md rule 6); the coaching session runs UTC, so leaving someone else's zone here silently mis-dates every evening entry.

baseline._comment: Set once, at intake, from the protocol in skills/intake Session 6. weightLb is REQUIRED by the validator even on charts with no body-composition domain — RMR needs it.

_provenance._comment: REQUIRED once this file exists: one entry per real key above, checked by scripts/test-provenance.mjs. Vocabulary and rules are in data/METHOD.md under 'Provenance'. Shape: { "class": "athlete-stated|athlete-confirmed|coach-proposed-unconfirmed|derived|external", "asOf": "YYYY-MM-DD", "source": "where the reasoning is written down", "note": "whose number this is, in prose" } — plus "quote" or "measured" for the athlete- classes, and "inputs" for derived. Never add a marker to a value you did not trace; an unmarked value is honest, a wrongly-marked one is not.

plan._comment: Current phase parameters. Only fill what this athlete's domains actually need — a chart with no energy domain does not need a calorie budget, and inventing one is the failure CLAUDE.md §1.1 exists to prevent. estMaintenanceKcal and proteinFloorG are validator-required. Optional keys the code reads if present, and ignores if absent: fatTargetG and fibreTargetG (written into each generated targets.csv row), weeklyAlcoholKcalBudget (subtracted from weeklyKcalBudget to give the food allowance — it sits INSIDE the calorie budget, never on top of it).

kcalByWeekday._comment: REQUIRED wherever a calorie target exists, and the reason it is a weekday map rather than one daily figure is that the unevenness is usually the plan — a bigger day parked where the athlete actually wants it. scripts/generate-targets.mjs writes one targets.csv row per day from this and EXITS NON-ZERO on any weekday it has no entry for, because a day without a target is the failure CLAUDE.md §0.3 and data/METHOD.md both call out by name. Seven entries, keyed exactly: Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun — CAPITALISED and three letters, because that is what every weekday lookup in the code produces. Seven right numbers under seven wrong names is a chart where every single day has no target, and validate-data.mjs now checks the KEYS rather than counting them. The validator additionally checks they sum to weeklyKcalBudget — a total that disagrees with its parts is a record contradicting itself. No example figures are given here on purpose: a calorie target is a decision about a person, and a plausible-looking placeholder is how one gets inherited. If this chart has no energy domain, delete this key and the daily-rollover workflow with it.

plan._max_rate_note: CLAUDE.md §5.2 hard floor. Do not raise it.
plan._adherenceRoutingPct_note: Not the athlete's number and not the coach's — it is CLAUDE.md §7's routing rule, so it ships filled in and its provenance class is `external`. Below this, a week routes to the adherence agent instead of the domain specialists, because a plan that is not being followed is not a programming problem. scripts/test-single-home.mjs checks that every document stating this figure states the same one; leave the value here and cite the key elsewhere rather than retyping 80.

_provenance._comment: REQUIRED once this file exists — see baseline._provenance above for the shape. A target the athlete is asked to hit is `coach-proposed-unconfirmed` until they have ruled on it in words about that number; adherence is not confirmation. Never invent a marker to clear the check, and never delete a value to make one go away. The two entries below ship filled in because their provenance is a fact about this system rather than about any athlete — they are also the worked example of the shape.

maxRatePctBwPerWk.source: CLAUDE.md §5.2, 'No sustained loss rate above 1.0% of bodyweight per week'
maxRatePctBwPerWk.note: The charter's safety floor, not this athlete's preference and not the coach's judgement. It ships with the template at 1.0 and is enforced against the athlete's own instruction; it is not negotiable downward by either party.

adherenceRoutingPct.source: CLAUDE.md §7, 'Route to adherence whenever completion falls below 80% for a week'
adherenceRoutingPct.note: The charter's routing rule. Nobody on this chart chose 80 — it ships with the template, and every document that states the figure is checked against this key by scripts/test-single-home.mjs so the four copies cannot drift apart.

triggers._comment: Machine-readable mirror of the trigger values in athlete/goals.md, so the dashboard can draw reference lines and the findings layer can fire. goals.md is authoritative for the reasoning; if the two disagree, goals.md wins and this is the bug. ONLY the keys named below are recognised — scripts/lib/findings.mjs and src/app/page.tsx read them by name, so a trigger invented under a different key renders nowhere and fires never. Every one is optional; a chart that measures none of these carries none of them. If this athlete's domains need a trigger with no key here, it needs code, not a new key — raise it rather than writing one that silently does nothing.

_recognised.waistTriggerIn: Goal line on the waist chart; fires a finding at or past it.
_recognised.waistWorkingBaselineIn: Reference line the waist trend is read against.
_recognised.weightCheckpointLb: A review checkpoint — fires a finding at or past it. Not a goal and not a floor.
_recognised.weightFloorLb: The deficit stops here regardless of anything else. Fires below it.

_provenance._comment: REQUIRED once this file exists — see baseline._provenance above. A threshold the athlete has not ruled on is `coach-proposed-unconfirmed`, and it stays live and marked rather than being deleted. Anything clinical belongs to their doctor: route it, never pick a number to close a gap.

domains._comment: The athlete/goals.md domain headings, VERBATIM, keyed by the role the code needs to name one for. This is the machine-readable pointer; goals.md holds the reasoning and the ranking. Without it, findings render with no domain label — which is honest, and is why there is no default: a default would be another chart's domain wearing this one's name. Roles the code asks for: `energyDeficit` (the domain a calorie deficit serves) and `health`. Add a key only when this chart actually has that domain.

sessionTypes._comment: WHAT THIS ATHLETE DOES, and what each activity costs, counts for, and serves. The list is the athlete's, not the system's: scripts/lib/schema.mjs derives training.csv's `type` enum from these keys, scripts/lib/athlete.mjs derives the MET table and the sessions-floor set, and the dashboard's /log form offers exactly these. AN ACTIVITY THAT IS NOT REGISTERED CAN ONLY BE LOGGED AS `other`, WHICH COUNTS TOWARD NOTHING — so an athlete who runs, and whose chart never registered running, trains six days a week and is invisible to the adherence count (audit F-15). `rest` and `other` are supplied by scripts/lib/athlete.mjs to every chart; do not register them, the validator rejects it. Required per entry: met (0-25), countsTowardFloor (true|false), domain (the goals.md heading it serves). Optional: note, metByIntensity ({light,moderate,hard} — used when a session logs its own minute split, so a long easy session is not priced at its hardest tier), energyCountedIn (name another column whose data already includes this activity's energy — then met MUST be 0, or it is counted twice), loading (true|false — DID THIS TIRE YOU OUT. A third question, not a restatement of the other two: countsTowardFloor asks whether it earns credit against the sessions/week floor, met asks whether it burns calories, and real registries come apart on all three. A rehab block can load genuinely while deliberately earning no floor credit; a walk priced at a real MET — which is correct on a chart with NO step feed, where nothing else counts that movement — may still be a rest day. Omit it and it defaults to `met > 0 and no energyCountedIn`, which is right for most entries; set it only where that default is wrong. It feeds the consecutive-loading-days count that tells a coach how hard the last few days have been).

<a walk, on a chart with no step feed>.note: The second entry exists to show the ONE case `loading` is for. With no step feed nothing else counts this movement, so it is priced as a session at a real MET — and the default would then call it loading and read a week of walks as a week with no rest day.

program._comment: The current block's weekly skeleton, so /today can show the planned session without waiting for a coaching session to hand-write a training.csv row. A real training.csv row ALWAYS wins over this. Rationale, exercise detail and autoregulation live in program/current-block.md; this is only the machine-readable outline, and a chart with no training domain does not need it at all. `weeklyTemplate` is keyed Mon|Tue|Wed|Thu|Fri|Sat|Sun — capitalised, three letters, same as plan.kcalByWeekday and for the same reason: `planDay()` looks the day up with that key, and a lower-cased map silently resolves to no session at all; `dailyRehabMin` is optional and only where a rehab block is running.

events._comment: Dated things worth counting down to: a trip, a procedure, an event the plan is built around.

copy._comment: Sentences the dashboard renders that are about THIS athlete — their measurement history, their block, their protocol. One of the four homes for athlete-specific language (scripts/check-no-athlete-leak.mjs), and it exists because shared components used to carry these as string literals, so every new chart inherited the previous athlete's tile labels and caveats (audit F-31). Every key is optional: a page with no entry renders a generic sentence or renders nothing, and that is a correct chart rather than a gap. NOTHING HERE MAY CARRY A NUMBER that has a home elsewhere — scripts/test-single-home.mjs checks prose figures against this file, and this key is prose. Keys the pages read: waistTileLabel, waistCardTitle, waistCardCaption, bodyFormCaption, templateFlexNote.

metrics._comment: Registry for anything tracked in data/metrics.csv — the long-format file for measures the fixed columns of body.csv don't cover. This is where a symptom count, a medication, a lab value or a device reading goes, in the athlete's own vocabulary, so a new chart never needs code edited to record a new thing. Every entry must name its unit, its direction (up|down = which way is progress), and the goals.md domain it serves. The validator rejects an entry with no domain, because a metric no domain needs is a chore the coach invented.
